{
  "approach": "query",
  "change": "Refactor app/db.py to optimize the list_notes function by replacing the INSTR-based tag filtering with a normalized many-to-many join table. 1) Add a new table 'note_tags' with columns (note_id INTEGER, tag TEXT) and a unique index on (note_id, tag). 2) Modify create_note to insert the note, then insert rows into note_tags for each tag. 3) Modify update_note to delete existing tags for the note_id and insert new ones. 4) Modify delete_note to delete associated note_tags. 5) Rewrite list_notes to use a JOIN between notes and note_tags for tag filtering (WHERE note_tags.tag = ?) and standard LIKE for search_text, using GROUP BY notes.id to handle duplicates from the join. This replaces the O(N*M) string search with an O(log N) index lookup.",
  "hypothesis": "The current profile shows list_notes is the hottest path, and the existing tag filtering uses INSTR(tags, ?) which performs a linear string scan on every row. By normalizing tags into a separate indexed table, tag lookups become index-based joins, which are significantly faster for SQLite, especially as the number of notes or tags grows. This reduces the cumulative time in list_notes by avoiding full-table string scans for tag matching.",
  "risks": [
    "Increased write complexity for create, update, and delete operations due to maintaining the join table.",
    "Potential for data inconsistency if transaction isolation is not strictly maintained (mitigated by using transactions).",
    "Schema migration requires adding a new table and indexes, which may take time on large databases (not applicable for this small-scale test but relevant for production)."
  ],
  "schema_version": 1
}
